dataset.name: Tropospheric NO2 (NASA SVS / Earth Information Center)
dataset.derivation: Recovered from the published colour bar of the EIC visual frames, not from the numeric product behind them. The bar is a mapping someone else defined and stated; this runs it backwards.

inversion_error.note: How accurately the colour bar inverts its own colours. This is the floor: a frame can be no more faithful than its own legend.

contract.note: 3.0 dB of spectral tilt per 1e15 molecules/cm2, level at 5.0. Both come from the published bar: the balance point is its middle and the slope spans 30.0 dB end to end.

grid.note: Rows and columns of the published frame. This visualization states no geographic bounds, so georeferencing it would mean inventing the one number that makes a map a map. The values are still recovered through the published colour bar; only their placement on the Earth is unclaimed.

axis.note: A still frame has no time axis, so the transport sweeps it north to south, sounding the area-weighted mean of each latitude band.

threshold_note: OKLab distance from the colour bar beyond which a pixel is treated as not data. Basemap, coastlines, labels and cloud land far from every colour on the bar; data pixels land on it. Marked pixels fall silent, so missing data never sounds like a low value.

verification.note: CHECK VALUES, NOT DATA. The player recomputes these in the browser from field.i16 and refuses to sound anything if they disagree.
verification.tolerance_note: Computed from the quantized payload - the same bytes the browser decodes - so the only disagreement this can catch is a real one.
verification.probes_note: Raw int16 values at known flat indices. A mismatch means the payload was decoded with the wrong endianness or layout.
